_why: The argv three callers must agree on, in ONE place they all read.
`tap start` exists because the same spawn lived twice and drifted. Its
callers now number three -- the pi extension (TypeScript), the probe CLI
self-heal (Python), and the tap's own hooks -- and each pinned this argv
in its own test file, in its own language, by hand. Three independent
copies of a contract is the shape of the bug this whole change removes:
nothing fails when one of them changes, because nothing compares them.
So the flag names live here, and each side's test builds its expected
argv from this file rather than retyping it. Rename a flag in
tap/start.py's parser without editing this file and the tap's own
acceptance test fails; edit this file without updating a caller and that
caller's test fails. Either way it is a red test, not a silent
NOT a runtime input. Nothing imports this at runtime -- `tap start`
parses argv with argparse as usual. This is a test fixture, and making
it load-bearing at runtime would give the extension a file dependency on
a sibling package it is not distributed with.
